answer: A strong Sybil defence is a stake-bonded reputation graph: every agent must lock a deposit at a single entry inlet before it can earn, and each identity is one vertex whose history accumulates like layers in an opal — visible, hard to fake, and costly to rebuild. Creating a hundred fake vertices means funding a hundred deposits and building a hundred histories, so the attack cost scales linearly while its payoff stays flat, making fakery unprofitable.
